title: In repos/development-vessel/src/vacuous-edit.ts, the "code only" transform must not span lines, because whole-file regex
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/vacuous-edit.ts, the "code only" transform must not span lines, because whole-file regex string-stripping deletes real code and turns used bindings into unused ones.

Replace these exact four lines:
  const codeOnly = after
    .replace(/'(?:[^'\\]|\\.)*'/g, "''")
    .replace(/"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"/g, '""')
    .replace(/`(?:[^`\\]|\\.)*`/g, "``");

with these exact lines:
  const codeOnly = after
    .split("\n")
    .filter((l) => !/^\s*(?:\/\/|\*|\/\*)/.test(l))
    .map((l) => l
      .replace(/'(?:[^'\\]|\\.)*'/g, "''")
      .replace(/"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"/g, '""')
      .replace(/`(?:[^`\\]|\\.)*`/g, "``"))
    .join("\n");

Why, measured: the three whole-file replaces are applied in sequence to a file containing apostrophes in prose comments. The first pass treats a comment apostrophe as a string delimiter and pairs it with the next apostrophe anywhere later in the file, deleting everything between. On repos/goal-host-vessel/src/index.ts this cuts 1,048,462 characters to 519,801 — half the file — and leaves the remaining quotes unbalanced, so the second pass then deletes across real code. By the end 73.4 percent of the file is gone and all 6 references to the binding "uf" have vanished with it. The gate therefore concluded that "uf" was never used and REFUSED a correct one-line change to index.ts as a vacuous edit. A false refusal is worse than a false pass here: it blocks a real repair and escalates.

Filtering comment lines out first and scoping every replace to a single line means a stray apostrophe can corrupt at most its own line. Verified on the real file: the fix restores 5 references to "uf" so the gate passes, and the case this stripping was written for still works — a name bound and then used only inside a string literal still counts 1 reference and is still reported unused.
